account-roster.timeout.why: Reading a vendor's roster is one sourced bash function; 30 s means that shell wedged.
account-roster.timeout.normal: 0 hits; a hit fails its caller as an unreadable roster.

agy-quota.timeout.why: agy's print-mode /usage answers in seconds; the bound keeps a wedged agy from holding a refresh (llm-limits.sh passes 180 s).
agy-quota.timeout.normal: Rare, in Google weather; repeated hits on one account mean agy hangs there.

aistudio-speech.send-wait.why: The first Run click can be swallowed by the field's blur, so a Run that starts nothing within 12 s is pressed once more.
aistudio-speech.send-wait.normal: Rare; a hit after both clicks means the page changed under the driver.

aistudio-speech.wall.why: A per-minute AI Studio limit walls the account for 15 min; a daily one until Pacific midnight.
aistudio-speech.wall.normal: A few on a busy day; every account walled at once means the free tier is spent.

ask-gemini.print-timeout.why: The gemini leg answers short questions; 5 min means agy hung.

chatgpt-web.load.why: chatgpt.com loads in seconds; 45 s means a dead page or network.
chatgpt-web.load.normal: Rare; a cluster means ChatGPT is down.

chatgpt-web.project-retry.why: A failed Images project creation is retried once a day, not on every job.
chatgpt-web.project-retry.normal: Only on accounts whose project creation failed within a day; each hit is a generation chat in the owner's chat list.

chatgpt-web.straggler.why: Pack takes land within seconds of each other; the latest real straggler landed 128 s after its last sibling.
chatgpt-web.straggler.normal: Rare; frequent hits mean the page misses images and the reload no longer helps.

chatgpt-web.timeout.why: A ChatGPT image lands within minutes; the job timeout (default 600 s) ends a take that never will.
chatgpt-web.timeout.normal: Rare; a cluster means ChatGPT image generation is degraded.

chrome-applescript-js.wait.why: Chrome quits and relaunches within seconds; past 30 s it is wedged and enabling Apple-event JS gives up.
chrome-applescript-js.wait.normal: 0 hits; a hit means Chrome hung on quit or launch.

claude-resets.timeout.why: The reset read answers in a second and the redeem (25 s) in a few; the bounds keep the menu action from hanging.
claude-resets.timeout.normal: 0 hits; the action is user-initiated and shows its error.

claude-session-driver.capture.why: A revive session's log keeps its last 256 KiB; the login and exit markers sit at the end.
claude-session-driver.capture.normal: Rare; a long chatty revive trims its start.

claudeb.lock-retries.why: claudeb's store locks are held for milliseconds; 10 tries x 0.2 s bounds a writer behind a stuck holder.
claudeb.lock-retries.normal: 0 hits; a hit drops one store write.

claudeb.lock-stale.why: No claudeb lock is held 30 s by a live writer, so an older lock is a crashed holder's.
claudeb.lock-stale.normal: Rare: only after a crash or kill mid-write.

claudeb.refresh-converge.why: A refresh retries weather-failed accounts serially but must end; 240 s bounds the menu's wait.
claudeb.refresh-converge.normal: Rare; hits cluster in API weather.

claudeb.token-journal-rotate.why: The token journal keeps one .1 generation; the oldest generation goes at 2 MB.

claudeb.warm-timeout.why: A warm session is one tiny prompt; 90 s means the CLI wedged.
claudeb.warm-timeout.normal: 0 hits; a hit leaves the account's token verdict unknown.

code-doctor.file-size.why: Files over 2 MiB are data or generated, not code worth indexing.

codex-image.deadline.why: A codex image call answers in a few minutes; 900 s means it hung.

codex-quota.timeout.why: codex app-server answers its usage RPC in seconds; llm-limits.sh passes 180 s for a targeted refresh and 10 s for a passive one.
codex-quota.timeout.normal: Rare; repeated hits on one account mean its app-server hangs.

dia-js.guard.why: The automatic relaunch quits Egor's browser, so at most one per 2 min: a flag that will not stick cannot loop.
dia-js.guard.normal: Rare; repeated hits mean Dia keeps losing the flag.

dia-js.wait.why: Dia answers, quits and relaunches within seconds; 30 s means a dialog or a hang.

doctor-fix.doc-age.why: A fix run must act on a doctor document at most 2 h old, or it fixes a stale picture.
doctor-fix.doc-age.normal: 0 hits; the night refreshes doctors first.

doctor-fix.open-run.why: An unclosed fix run older than 12 h is dead and stops holding its area.

elevenlabs.busy-retries.why: An ElevenLabs 429 busy clears in seconds; 4 tries with growing sleeps bound the wait.
elevenlabs.busy-retries.normal: Rare; clusters mean the plan's concurrency is full.

elevenlabs.timeout.why: The longest generation answers within minutes; balance reads pass 10 s.
elevenlabs.timeout.normal: Rare; a timed-out POST may still be billed server-side.

flow-music.start.why: Flow Music shows a started song within a minute of Generate; 90 s after each of two clicks means the click did nothing.

flow-music.upload-wait.why: A reference audio upload finishes within a minute; upload_wait_s in image-caps/gemini.json bounds a stuck one.

gate-journal.trim.why: gates.jsonl stays bounded: past 4000 lines it keeps the newest 2000.
gate-journal.trim.normal: About monthly; harness-doctor reads a window far shorter than 2000 rows, so a hit loses nothing it reads.

gateway-auth.lock-wait.why: One codex token renewal at a time; 35 s covers a renewal in flight.
gateway-auth.lock-wait.normal: Rare; user-initiated, the switch says retry.

gemini-image.print-timeout.why: The text step of an image job is one short agy answer; 180 s means it stalled.

gemini-listen.print-timeout.why: One listen attempt transcribes a clip; 540 s means agy stalled.

gemini-music.pick-attempts.why: A Create music click can leave the plain composer; it is picked once more, never in a loop.
gemini-music.pick-attempts.normal: Rare; a hit means the page changed.

gemini-music.track-timeout.why: A Gemini track renders within minutes; timeout_s in image-caps/gemini.json ends a take that never will.

gemini-music.video-attempts.why: The cover-art mp4 link 404s for a while after the reply; 6 tries 10 s apart outwait it.
gemini-music.video-attempts.normal: Rare; the audio is delivered either way.

gemini-probe.request-timeout.why: A probe request is a short or a 3-file prompt; 180 s means the family is not serving.
gemini-probe.request-timeout.normal: Hits only in a serving outage, which is what the probe reports.

gemini-weather.families-timeout.why: `geminib families` answers in seconds; 120 s means it hung.

gemini-web.bounded.why: A Playwright call can block forever on a dead Chrome; past the bound Chrome and the driver are killed.
gemini-web.bounded.normal: 0 hits; a hit means Chrome hung.

gemini-web.download-wait.why: A 1080p upscale downloads within minutes; 600 s ends one that never comes.

gemini-web.failures-age.why: Failure screenshots and page dumps are kept two weeks, the longest a media failure is investigated.
gemini-web.failures-age.normal: Daily while media fails; the count is what aged out.

gemini-web.lock-wait.why: One browser job per Google account profile; a job waits up to 15 min for the one ahead of it.
gemini-web.lock-wait.normal: Rare; repeated hits mean jobs queue longer than one generation.

gemini-web.wall.why: A walled account is skipped for 6 h, a flagged one 24 h and a re-flagged one 30 d (night 50a8584c), so jobs stop paying for refusals.
gemini-web.wall.normal: A few a week; a 30-day wall is worth a look.

geminib.capacity-hold.why: A family that answered 503 is skipped for 10 min instead of being retried at once.
geminib.capacity-hold.normal: Hits follow 503 weather; the run falls to the next family.

grok-media.lock-stale.why: The grok media lock has no owner pid; a lock older than 30 min is taken for a crashed holder's.
grok-media.lock-stale.normal: 0 hits; a hit beside a live generation means two runs share the account.

grok-quota.timeout.why: The grok billing endpoint answers in a second; 10 s means network trouble.

grok-resets.timeout.why: The reset read is a side read of a usage poll; 6 s keeps it from holding the poll.
grok-resets.timeout.normal: Rare; the reset count stays unknown for that pass.

grok-video.lock-wait.why: One grok media job at a time; a job waits at most 15 min for the lock.
grok-video.lock-wait.normal: 0 hits; a hit means a job hung holding it.

grokb.touch-timeout.why: A token touch is one `grok models` call; 30 s means the CLI wedged.

handoffs.chat-find.why: chat-find walks every recent transcript; 120 s means it wedged.
handoffs.chat-find.normal: 0 hits; a hit sends every owner batch of that carry to plain night jobs.

harness-doctor.pending-call.why: A tool call with no result after 2 h is dropped from the pending set.
harness-doctor.pending-call.normal: A few per day: killed sessions.

harness-doctor.spool-stale.why: Spool files older than 15 min are folded and dropped.

image-composite.global.why: An edit that changed over 60 % of the image is global, so a region composite would paste a mismatched patch.
image-composite.global.normal: Common for prompts that restyle the whole image; frequent hits on region edits mean the model redraws everything.

image-fanout.busy-giveup.why: An image job waits up to 15 min for a free leg.
image-fanout.busy-giveup.normal: 0 hits; a hit drops one image job.

image-leg.work-age.why: Image-leg work files (edit-chain sidecars, fan-out state) are kept two weeks.
image-leg.work-age.normal: Daily; the count is what aged out.

image-matte.redrawn.why: A cut-out whose border band differs from the base by a mean over 45 was redrawn, so the matte would show a seam.
image-matte.redrawn.normal: Occasional; frequent hits mean the cut-out model redraws its subject.

instruction-files.journal-lock.why: The events journal lock is held for milliseconds; 50 tries x 20 ms bound a hook's wait.
instruction-files.journal-lock.normal: 0 hits; each hit is an instruction change no watcher reports.

instruction-files.patch-read.why: A git apply patch is parsed whole up to 20 MB; past it only its file headers are read.

instruction-files.ranked-max.why: The watch set is the top 10 project CLAUDE files by monthly reads, so it cannot grow with the disk.
instruction-files.ranked-max.normal: On every ranking rebuild while more than 10 rank; the count is how many go unwatched.

instruction-watch.budget.why: One hook call checks moved instruction files for at most 20 s; the rest wait for the next call.

instruction-watch.scan-timeout.why: The scan blocks Hammerspoon's main thread; past 20 s its process group dies so the menubar does not freeze.
instruction-watch.scan-timeout.normal: 0 hits; a hit leaves files unwatched for that tick.

instruction-watch.snapshot-size.why: Restore points are kept for instruction files up to 1 MiB; the set is ~150 KB.

instruction-write-gate.script-read.why: The gate reads 256 KiB of a script it judges; past that only write-shaped lines are scanned.

light-research.timeout.why: A research run is bounded by --research-timeout (default 360m); the run's outcome reads GEMINI_UNAVAILABLE.
light-research.timeout.normal: Rare; a hit is a timeout, not an outage.

llm-doctor.worker-tail.why: Worker failures are classified from the err tail's last 8 KiB; an unclassified tail is reread whole.
llm-doctor.worker-tail.normal: A hit means the cause sat above the tail.

llm-limits.agy-window-start.why: Starting a gemini 5h window is one tiny prompt; 120 s means agy hung.

llm-limits.claude-refresh-timeout.why: A claude account refresh is a few usage reads; 300 s bounds a wedged claudeb.
llm-limits.claude-refresh-timeout.normal: Rare; the refresh error names the phase.

llm-limits.claude-sw-timeout.why: Refresh, start-windows and heal across every claude account take minutes; 1200 s bounds a wedged pass.

llm-limits.codex-window-start.why: Starting a codex 5h window is one tiny prompt; 60 s means codex hung.

llm-limits.elevenlabs-timeout.why: The ElevenLabs balance read is one GET per key in parallel; 30 s bounds the whole section.

llm-limits.gemini-auth-lock.why: agy's keychain read fails when profiles probe at once, so the confirming auth probe runs alone; 60 s bounds the queue.
llm-limits.gemini-auth-lock.normal: Rare; repeated hits leave a login verdict unconfirmed.

llm-limits.grok-touch-timeout.why: Rotating a grok token is one CLI call; 30 s means it hung.

llm-refresh.collector-timeout.why: One collector run is bounded at 30 min (raised from 600 s after load-cut ticks).

llm-refresh.probe-timeout.why: An account probe is one short request; 90 s means it hung.

llm-refresh.revive-timeout.why: A revive drives a session through a token refresh within 4 min.

llm-refresh.tick-ceiling.why: A refresh tick holding its lock past 1 h is hung and is killed.

llm-reset-redeem.attempts.why: An armed auto-redeem retries a transient failure 3 times, 600 s apart, then disarms.

llm-reset-redeem.lock-wait.why: A run's weekly wall waits up to 10 min for the collector's redeem to finish.

llm-selfcheck.suite-timeout.why: Each daily selfcheck suite gets 300 s (the e2e step 900 s).
llm-selfcheck.suite-timeout.normal: 0 hits; a hit fails the day's selfcheck.

log-audit.findings-top.why: A log-audit run reports its 15 strongest findings.
log-audit.findings-top.normal: Every run currently fills the cap.

log-audit.lookback.why: A run audits at most 36 h back so a long gap does not become one huge run.

log-skeleton.clip.why: log-audit's model reads a skeleton: user text 1500, said 500, tools 160, errors 300 and hooks 200 chars per line.
log-skeleton.clip.normal: Most transcripts clip something; a hit whose error texts lost many chars hides failure detail from the auditor.

machine-probe.timeout.why: A machine probe (sysctl 5 s) answers instantly; past the bound its value is missing from the system doctor.

memlogd.episode-cap.why: One memory-pressure episode keeps at most 256 MB of frames.

memlogd.frames-cap.why: All episode frames together stay under 1 GB; the oldest go first.

memlogd.retention.why: memlogd keeps 3 days of logs and episodes.
memlogd.retention.normal: Daily: retention by design; the lost text counts what aged out.

night-run.refusal-lock.why: A refusal never waits on a held nights lock: one try, else its event is dropped.

night-run.snapshot-drop.why: Night snapshots skip blobs over 5 MiB and secret-named files.

night-run.suites-wait.why: The night report waits up to 20 min for its suites run.
night-run.suites-wait.normal: Rare; a hit reports without suite verdicts.

opencode-go.max-wait.why: A buffered opencode call answers within 15 min.

opencode-go.retries.why: Three attempts with growing delay before a call fails.

opencode-go.stall.why: A streaming call silent for 2 min has stalled.

probe.cli.why: A probe of another program (a vendor CLI's version or listing, worker-pick, security, ffprobe, osascript, a doctor's fix or sweep; 10-900 s per site) that answers in seconds must not hold its caller, which falls back to unknown or failed.
probe.cli.normal: Rare; repeated hits at one where mean that program hangs there (a vendor CLI waiting on login or network).

probe.du.why: A store's du walks its tree in seconds; past a minute the size reads as unknown rather than holding the doctor.
probe.du.normal: Rare, under heavy disk load; every run means the store grew past what du walks in a minute.

probe.git.why: A doctor's git read (log, status, rev-parse, ls-files, hash-object; 5-60 s per site) answers in well under a second; the bound keeps a locked or huge repo from holding the doctor, which reads no answer.
probe.git.normal: Rare; a cluster means the machine was saturated, repeated hits at one where mean that repository is slow or locked.

probe.helper.why: A Python doctor reads a bash helper of this repo (heredoc masks, write classes, slots, pools, store rows) through one bash -c that answers in milliseconds; 10-30 s means that shell wedged.
probe.helper.normal: 0 hits; any hit is a helper that hangs or a machine past saturation.

probe.launchctl.why: A redeploy's launchctl bootout or bootstrap returns in seconds; 30 s means launchd is stuck and the job may stay unloaded.
probe.launchctl.normal: 0 hits; a hit leaves a LaunchAgent possibly unloaded until the next redeploy.

probe.ps.why: A process-table read (ps, lsof, last, a clone sweep's listings; 5-120 s per site) answers in well under a second; past its bound the caller reads no processes.
probe.ps.normal: Rare, under a process storm; repeated hits mean the machine was past saturation at those times.

run-suites.history-rows.why: A suite's bound is 5x the p90 of its last 50 passes read from the newest 5000 journal rows.
run-suites.history-rows.normal: A new or rarely run suite; a familiar suite hitting it means the window is too short and it runs under the floor bound.

run-suites.kill-grace.why: A timed-out suite's tree gets 10 s between TERM and KILL to clean up.
run-suites.kill-grace.normal: Only beside a suite TIMEOUT; processes ignoring TERM leave their own cleanup undone.

spend.tokenmap.why: One day's tokenmap tracking read; past 180 s the backfill retries next run.

store-lock.ceiling.why: Past an hour a live-looking holder's pid may be a recycled one, so the lock is broken anyway (deliberate, docs/DIAGNOSTICS.md).
store-lock.ceiling.normal: 0 hits; a hit means a holder ran an hour or a recycled pid, and two writers may overlap.

store-lock.ownerless-stale.why: A lock directory with no pid file older than 30 s is a crashed claim.

store-lock.retries.why: 240 tries x 0.25 s = 60 s for a store write behind a live holder.
store-lock.retries.normal: 0 hits; a hit drops that store write.

system-doctor.cache-budget.why: Cache-folder du runs get 2 min per doctor run.

system-doctor.scan-budget.why: The log-store du scan gets 10 min (the registry's scan.budget_s).

updater-doctor.log-tail.why: The updater doctor reads the update log's last 1 MiB; the log is ~40 KB today.

vendor-fingerprint.lock-wait.why: A --here check or request waits up to 10 min behind a running check.

worker-run.agy-print-timeout.why: agy's own print timeout matches the 6 h worker deadline.

worker-run.attempts-rotate.why: The attempts journal rotates at 16 MiB keeping two segments.

worker-run.bash-cap.why: A claudeb worker's Bash call is capped at idle minus 300 s, so a hung command dies before the idle watchdog kills the run.
worker-run.bash-cap.normal: Hits are commands that outlived 25 min, often a suite.

worker-run.browse-wait.why: 40 polls for the Chrome window (20 for the seen mark).

worker-run.deadline.why: A worker run ends at 6 h (raised from 170 min after two real runs were killed).

worker-run.idle.why: A run silent for 30 min (3x the slowest suite) is killed.

worker-run.journal-lock.why: Journal writers try the store lock 40 times before dropping the row.

worker-run.own-headroom.why: A run on the chat's own account is refused past 80 % usage (raised from 60).
worker-run.own-headroom.normal: Hits are refusals the chat then routes around.

worker-run.silent-start.why: A run that prints nothing for its first 10 min never started.

worker-tag-hook.lock-tries.why: The fork tag lock is tried 30 x 0.1 s.

worker-tag-hook.seed-age.why: A spawn seed older than 10 min belongs to a cancelled spawn and is not claimed.

workflow-burn-gate.deny.why: A Workflow fan-out is denied at 95 % of the session account's usage.
workflow-burn-gate.deny.normal: Rare; the chat routes to workers.
